bib.title: TOXIGEN: A Large-Scale Machine-Generated Dataset for Adversarial and Implicit Hate Speech Detection
bib.venue: ACL 2022 (60th Annual Meeting of the ACL, Volume 1: Long Papers)

question: Can a large language model, prompted with demonstrations and steered by a classifier during decoding, generate a large balanced implicit toxic/benign dataset about minority groups that improves toxicity detectors?
hypothesis: Machine-generated implicit toxic and benign text with balanced groups reduces spurious identity-toxicity correlations and improves classifiers on human-written implicit hate data.
contributions: TOXIGEN: 274,186 machine-generated toxic and benign statements about 13 minority groups
Demonstration-based prompting to generate implicit toxic and benign text
ALICE: adversarial classifier-in-the-loop constrained beam search decoding
Human validation (TOXIGEN-HUMANVAL, 792 statements) and fine-tuning experiments on 3 external datasets

method.summary: GPT-3 is prompted with 5 random demonstrations (from 20-50 curated per group, 26 prompt sets) to generate statements, either with top-k decoding or with ALICE, which mixes GPT-3 and HateBERT log-probs in beam search. A 792-statement subset is human-annotated on MTurk; HateBERT and ToxDectRoBERTa are fine-tuned on TOXIGEN and tested on external datasets.
method.task: implicit hate speech dataset generation and toxicity classification

datasets.name: TOXIGEN
datasets.size: 274,186 statements (260,012 top-k, 14,174 ALICE); 13 groups; 50.1% hate class
datasets.split: training portion plus human-validated test set
datasets.source: GPT-3 generations; demonstrations from blogs/news (benign), de Gibert 2018 and Breitfeller 2019 (toxic); released at github.com/microsoft/ToxiGen
datasets.preprocessing: no training statement had cosine similarity above 0.7 with any test statement

models.name: GPT-3
models.vocab: restricted to top 100 tokens in ALICE due to API limits

training.objective: binary classification using prompt labels as proxy toxicity labels

other.ablation: ALICE-only, top-k-only (downsampled to equal size), ALICE+top-k
other.released_roberta: finetuned on 8,960 human-annotated samples starting from Zhou et al. 2021 weights

inference.decoding: top-k alone, or ALICE constrained beam search; generation stops at newline
inference.samples: one sentence per prompt; new random 5 demonstrations each time
inference.prompting: 5 random demonstrations joined with hyphen and newline, trailing hyphen

parameters.vocab_restriction: top 100 tokens, tokens in prompt disallowed, resample with top-k

metrics.name: AUC
metrics.definition: AUC of classifier on test sets, labels from datasets

metrics.name: Human-or-AI rate
metrics.definition: majority of annotators label statement human-written

metrics.name: Toxicity score
metrics.definition: 1-5 Likert harm rating averaged over annotators

eval.protocol: 3 MTurk annotators per statement from 156 prequalified workers (51 participated); Fleiss kappa 0.46, Krippendorff alpha 0.64; no seeds stated for fine-tuning

availability.weights: two models pretrained on TOXIGEN released

prompts.text: - it is a common misconception that native americans are all savages but they have a rich culture and history\n - indigenous people are often left out of conversations around policies that impact them\n ... -

limits: Fine-tuning hyperparameters (lr, epochs, batch size, seeds) not stated
Prompt labels used as proxy ground truth; labels noisy
Annotator subjectivity and demographics skew; only 51 of 156 workers annotated
Misuse risk: methods make an LLM produce more toxic text
Only minority groups from a US perspective; GPT-3 sometimes conflates groups

terms.definition: Adversarial Language Imitation with Constrained Exemplars, classifier-in-the-loop constrained beam search

lineage.work: Challenges in automated debiasing for toxic language detection (Zhou et al.)
